title: Raising the chromatic number at girth at least six
statement: Let $k \ge 2$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a finite graph on a nonempty vertex set whose chromatic number equals $k$ and whose girth is at least $6$. Then there exists a finite graph $H$ whose chromatic number is at least $k+1$ and whose girth is at least $6$.
hypotheses_covered: chromatic number of G equals k
girth of G is at least 6
replaced:
\emph{ (B\&M \S{}8.5, verbatim; B. Descartes).  }Let \texttt{G} be a
\texttt{k}-chromatic graph of girth at least six (\texttt{k $\ge$ 2}).  Form a new graph \texttt{H} as
follows: Take \texttt{C(k$\nu$, $\nu$)} disjoint copies of \texttt{G} and a set
\texttt{S} of \texttt{k$\nu$} new vertices,
and set up a one--one correspondence between the copies of \texttt{G} and the
\texttt{$\nu$}-element
subsets of \texttt{S}. For each copy of \texttt{G}, join its vertices to the members of
the
corresponding \texttt{$\nu$}-element subset of \texttt{S} by a matching. Show that
\texttt{H} has chromatic
number at least \texttt{k + 1} and girth at least six.*
